messages:
Sam W.: Heads-up: we observed a pinned session still routed to a variant after the retire_at window. Breaks the assumption that retire_at immediately stops traffic. Full repro logs attached in thread. We should formalize lifecycle signals.

Aisha: Can you drop the manifest fragment that caused it?

Sam W.: heres the snippet we pushed:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-redwood-v2",
  "variant": "f16-q4",
  "pinned": true,
  "retire_at": 1705000000,
  "soft_deprecate": true
}
```
Router logs: client session pinned earlier, runtime never re-evaluated retired status mid-session so kept routing.

Jun K.: Root cause: we leak two semantically overlapping fields (soft_deprecate + retire_at) and different components interpret them differently. Also the session/lease semantics are vague.

Toni: Suggest we replace ad-hoc signals with a small lifecycle enum + a few control knobs so both control-plane and runtime have deterministic behavior. Draft schema idea:
```json
"lifecycle": {
  "phase": "active",    // active | deprecated | draining | retired
  "effective_at": 1705000000, // when phase transition becomes authoritative
  "cache_ttl_seconds": 86400, // how long cached prefixes are honored for pinned sessions
  "session_lease_seconds": 3600, // short token lifetime for pinned sessions
  "pin_scope": "tenant"   // none | tenant | system
}
```
This makes it explicit: deprecated = no new auto-pins; draining = reject new sessions but honor existing leases until their expiry (or cache_ttl).
retired = no serving.

Aisha: Two practical questions: 1) should deprecated phase still execute inference on existing sessions? 2) how do we avoid thundering herd on cache eviction?

Jun K.: Operational semantics proposal: deprecated -> allow existing sessions; new session creation requires explicit tenant pin; draining -> start rejecting non-tenant pins, initiate soft cache eviction respecting cache_ttl_seconds for pinned leases; retired -> stop serving and mark tombstone. Add an optional per-tenant cache override to avoid one-size-fits-all.

Sam W.: To make runtime enforceable, control plane should issue short-lived session_lease tokens when a pin is created or refreshed. Runtime validates the token and can refuse to route when lease expired or phase prohibits it. Leases also let us force-expire pins by revoking tokens from control plane side.

Toni: Good. Also need an emergency path: force_retire flag that immediately flips to retired. Must be guarded (RBAC + two-person approval) and always create an audit event. We'll include force_retire reason and an undo window where possible.

ops-oncall: +1 on audit trail. For runbook: default cadence = deprecated for 48h, draining for 12h, retired thereafter. cache_ttl_seconds default to 24h for pinned sessions unless tenant requests less. Emergency retired cases require two on-call approvals and a postmortem within 72h.

Aisha: Backwards compatibility: clients that only look at retire_at should continue to work: if lifecycle absent, treat retire_at as effective_at->retired. Migration plan: v3+ clients read lifecycle.phase primarily; older clients read retire_at until EOL.

Jun K.: We also need an atomic state-diff RPC between control plane and runtime to avoid a window where control-plane believes variant is draining while runtime still sees it as active. Use versioned epoch + monotonic increment; runtime applies updates idempotently.

Sam W.: Example of a full manifest with lifecycle and a lease token example for the RFC:
```json
{
  "model_id": "gpt-redwood-v2",
  "variant": "f16-q4",
  "pinned": true,
  "lifecycle": {
    "phase": "draining",
    "effective_at": 1705000000,
    "cache_ttl_seconds": 86400,
    "session_lease_seconds": 1800,
    "pin_scope": "tenant"
  },
  "session_lease_token": "lease:v1:abcd1234"
}
```
Runtime verifies lease:v1 while routing. Control-plane can rotate tokens to revoke pins quickly.

Toni: Action items: I'll draft the RFC with the lifecycle definition + sample manifests + runbook and open for review. @infra-bot / @migrator-bot to prepare a migration job that annotates existing variants with a default lifecycle (active -> deprecated -> draining -> retired) and issues lease tokens for currently pinned sessions.

migrator-bot: migration job scheduled: 2026-04-16T03:30Z. Defaults: deprecated=48h, draining=12h, cache_ttl_seconds=86400.

ops-oncall: Also will prepare an emergency-retire checklist and RBAC change request.

Jun K.: Tests to add: unit tests for lifecycle transition table, integration test where control-plane flips to draining while runtime has many active leases, and a chaos test forcing force_retire during high load.

Aisha: We should also document tenant expectations: "tenant-scoped pins" survive through draining + cache_ttl but not after retired; tenants wanting longer must create a new pin on a supported variant. We'll include SLA language in the RFC.

Sam W.: TL;DR decisions agreed: 1) introduce lifecycle.phase enum + effective_at; 2) add cache_ttl_seconds and session_lease_seconds; 3) add pin_scope for tenant/system granularity; 4) implement short-lived lease tokens and token rotation for revocation; 5) support force_retire with RBAC/audit; 6) back-compat: fallback to retire_at when lifecycle missing.

Toni: I'll submit the RFC draft by EOD and attach runbook snippets.

infra-bot: annotator job queued and will emit events to #eng-runtime when migration starts.

ops-oncall: Runbook review scheduled Thursday 15:00 PT. :thumbsup:
